observed_original_abi.return_type_rationale: The SDK/Ghidra signature declares void and the listing agrees: the only writes to EAX are 0x0067e744 (the table load) and 0x0067e754 (the 0x00921580 result), and both are consumed by the loop, so no exit path produces a defined value. The reconstruction therefore models the target as a procedure.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: EAX carries no defined value on any exit path; the only writes to EAX are the vtable load at 0x0067e744 and the 0x00921580 result consumed into ESI at 0x0067e754. The function is a procedure, not a value producer.

ordinary_stack_arguments.note: 0x0067e73d MOV EBX,dword ptr [ESP + 0x10] addresses entry_ESP+0x4 because PUSH ESI (0x0067e730), PUSH EDI (0x0067e734) and PUSH EBX (0x0067e73c) have moved ESP from entry_ESP to entry_ESP-0xC. It is read exactly once, before the loop head at 0x0067e741, and the back edge at 0x0067e75b targets the head, so the word is hoisted out of the loop.

indirect_call_arguments.argument_order: 0x0067e749 PUSH EBX then 0x0067e74a PUSH 0x0, so the literal zero lands at [ESP+0] and the hoisted event word at [ESP+0x4]
indirect_call_arguments.stack_cleanup: callee; forced by the loop, since nothing between 0x0067e74c and the back edge drops the eight bytes this call pushes, so a per-iteration ESP growth is the only alternative and it cannot be what the body does

mechanics.kind: ungated observer-chain dispatch with a literal-zero leading argument
mechanics.chain_terminator: the ADDRESS of the embedded field at 0x4c, never its value
reads: dword [ECX+0x10] (as [ESI+0x10]) once per iteration, the node's receiver word
dword [ECX] once per iteration, the receiver's table word

never_read: the four bytes stored at 0x4c; the body takes the field's address with LEA at 0x0067e735 and never loads it, so the terminator's stored value is inert
mechanics.loop_invariant_hoist: The single stack argument is loaded into EBX at 0x0067e73d, before the loop head at 0x0067e741; the back edge at 0x0067e75b targets the head, so the load happens exactly once on the loop entry path and every iteration reuses the same word.
mechanics.successor_fetched_after_dispatch: 0x0067e74c CALL EDX precedes 0x0067e74f CALL 0x00921580, so a dispatch that mutates the chain is observed by the same run: the successor is whatever the stepper returns after the call, not a link captured before it.
mechanics.terminator_is_embedded: ECX+0x4c is inside the object, so the chain is closed by storage in the manager itself rather than by a null pointer or a separate sentinel pointer.
mechanics.flag_evidence: 0x0067e74a PUSH 0x0 -- the immediate is literally zero, distinct from the sibling entry's 0x0067e710 PUSH 0x1.
mechanics.per_iteration_reload: The receiver word (0x0067e741), its table word (0x0067e744) and the table entry (0x0067e746) are all loaded inside the loop, so consecutive nodes may dispatch through different tables. The model test pins this with two different entries in one chain.

callees.observed_shape: Not a fixed next-field read. 0x00921580 branches on the node's first word: if it is non-null (0x00921584) it walks the +0x4 chain to its last element (loop 0x00921591..0x00921598); if it is null (0x0092159b) it reads the node's +0x8 word and walks that structure (0x009215a2..0x009215ad), returning either the walked pointer or the starting node.

differences: The sibling tests byte [ECX+0x64] and returns immediately when it is clear; this entry has no such test and reaches the chain unconditionally.
The sibling pushes 0x1 as the leading dispatch argument (0x0067e710); this entry pushes 0x0 (0x0067e74a).
Both share the same chain walk, the same +0x4c address-taken terminator, the same +0x10 receiver word, the same +0x1c dispatch entry, the same EBX hoist and the same RET 0x4.
sibling_contrast.inference: The two entries are the same traversal parameterised by a boolean, and in one variant by the +0x64 byte. The evidence fixes the two flag values and the presence of the gate; it does not fix what the boolean means.

corroboration.decompiler_vs_listing: agreement on the traversal, disagreement on the receiver. The decompilation prints (**(code **)(**(int **)(iVar1 + 0x10) + 0x1c))(0,this), where its 'this' is the manager; the listing shows ECX holding the node's +0x10 word at 0x0067e741 and never reloading ECX from the manager inside the loop, so the 'this' of the indirect call is the node's receiver word, not the manager.
decompiler_caveats: The decompiler prints 'in_ECX' as a separate local and 'this' as a stack parameter; ECX is the receiver and the stack slot is the one ordinary argument. The listing settles this.

The decompiler renders the leading argument as a bare 0 and does not show the trailing argument at all; the listing shows PUSH EBX (the hoisted entry_ESP+0x4 word) at 0x0067e749 and PUSH 0x0 at 0x0067e74a, so there are two stack words, not one.
The decompiler's for-loop increment reads FUN_00921580(iVar1) with no stack adjustment shown; 0x0067e756 ADD ESP,0x4 is the caller-side cleanup that makes the call cdecl.
The 'WARNING: Unknown calling convention' is consistent with a __thiscall entry whose prototype carries an unannotated callee-cleaned stack word: RET 0x4 with the receiver in ECX.
gaps: The briefing's evidence lists DECOMPILATION, DISASSEMBLY and the Ghidra function record as missing; they were read live during this session and are cited individually above. The orchestrator also persisted no callers, globals, types or field offsets for this target, so every such fact here comes from the live bridge and the raw bytes.
No ABI projection was persisted for this target; the ABI in this sidecar is derived from the listing, and the derivation is spelled out instruction by instruction in observed_original_abi.

unresolved_questions: What is the concrete type behind the node's +0x10 receiver word, and what does its table entry at +0x1c do with the leading zero and the event word?
What is the intended meaning of the leading argument, given only that this entry passes 0 and its sibling 0x0067e6f0 passes 1 from the same walk?
What does the +0x64 byte that the sibling gates on mean, and is the pair an enable/disable or a register/unregister traversal?
What is 0x00921580 semantically? The listing shows two walks -- a +0x4 chain to its last element, and a +0x8 structure -- but nothing names it, and it is not this target.
Does the manager's own word at +0x4c ever hold a value another function uses, given that this body only address-takes it?
Which concrete subtype dispatches through vtable 0x01401b74, and who calls slot 17? There is no direct caller and the executable carries no RTTI.
Is the callee-cleaned eight-byte stack of the +0x1c entry confirmed anywhere, or is it only forced by the requirement that ESP stay constant across iterations?
runtime_gates: A live cCheatManager with a populated observer chain is required to observe the dispatch at all; the chain head at +0x50 must differ from the embedded terminator at +0x4c, or the body exits at 0x0067e73a without making any call.
The function is reachable only through vtable 0x01401b74 slot 17, so a differential run must construct that exact table and dispatch the slot.
The concrete receiver type must be identified before the +0x1c entry can be attributed a meaning, and before a stub with the right stack discipline can be confirmed.
notes: Reconstructed from the 24-instruction body, its raw bytes and the listings of its one direct callee and its containing vtable. The reconstruction is total for this body: every instruction, displacement, branch, register and return of 0x0067e730..0x0067e762 is accounted for, and nothing is asserted beyond it. Two details the prior package did not spell out are pinned here: the empty-chain JZ at 0x0067e73a targets POP EDI and so deliberately skips POP EBX, and the successor is fetched after the dispatch, which the model test demonstrates by unlinking the chain from inside the first dispatch. The callee is routed through a port table so the test can substitute a stub; the VA is kept in the port field name and no pointer value is invented. Where the decompilation and the listing disagree about the receiver and the argument count, the listing wins and the disagreement is recorded in corroboration.
